You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 13a9d08c296228d18289de60b83792c586e1d073 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Aug 2022 18:00:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] net: lan966x: improve error handle in
 lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame()

Don't just print a warning.  Clean up and return an error as well.

Fixes: c8349639324a ("net: lan966x: Add FDMA functionality")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Horatiu Vultur <horatiu.vultur@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/YwjgDm/SVd5c1tQU@kili
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
index 6dea7f8c1481..51f8a0816377 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
@@ -425,7 +425,8 @@ static struct sk_buff *lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame(struct lan966x_rx *rx)
 	lan966x_ifh_get_src_port(skb->data, &src_port);
 	lan966x_ifh_get_timestamp(skb->data, &timestamp);
 
-	WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports);
+	if (WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports))
+		goto free_skb;
 
 	skb->dev = lan966x->ports[src_port]->dev;
 	skb_pull(skb, IFH_LEN * sizeof(u32));
@@ -449,6 +450,8 @@ static struct sk_buff *lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame(struct lan966x_rx *rx)
 
 	return skb;
 
+free_skb:
+	kfree_skb(skb);
 unmap_page:
 	dma_unmap_page(lan966x->dev, (dma_addr_t)db->dataptr,
 		       FDMA_DCB_STATUS_BLOCKL(db->status),
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `lan966x_fdma.c`**
1. **Error Handling Improvement**: The patch modifies the error handling in the function `lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame`. 
   - The original code used `WARN_ON` to check if `src_port` is out of bounds, which only printed a warning without proper error handling.
   - The updated code changes this to an `if` statement that checks the condition and, if true, jumps to a cleanup section (`free_skb`).
   
2. **Memory Cleanup**: A new cleanup section is introduced:
   - If the `src_port` is invalid, the code now calls `kfree_skb(skb)` to free the allocated socket buffer before exiting the function.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification enhances the robustness of the error handling by not only warning about the invalid `src_port` but also ensuring that resources (the socket buffer) are properly released in case of an error. This change prevents potential memory leaks and improves the overall stability of the function. The relationship between the warning and the cleanup is that the warning is now part of a conditional check that leads to a more graceful error handling process.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports);
```
```c
skb = build_skb(page_address(page), PAGE_SIZE << rx->page_order);
```
```c
return skb;
```
Reason:
The original implementation only printed a warning when `src_port` was out of bounds, which did not prevent the function from proceeding to use the potentially invalid `src_port`. This could lead to undefined behavior or memory leaks, as the function would return an invalid socket buffer (`skb`) without properly cleaning up allocated resources.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports))
    goto free_skb;
```
```c
kfree_skb(skb);
```
Reason:
The patch introduces a check that, if `src_port` is out of bounds, it jumps to the `free_skb` label to clean up the allocated socket buffer (`skb`) before returning `NULL`. This ensures that resources are properly released, preventing memory leaks and undefined behavior.
